title: Saving The Last Dance For Mom

contact_edits.before: The play bears a fortuitous resemblance to Pedro Almodovar's Volver; both have estranged generations of women finding reconciliation, skeletons in family cupboards (more numerous and extreme in the movie) and a mother with a musical past, though the Spanish one's talent is for singing rather than dancing. It's unfair to compare a beginning playwright with a brilliant director at the height of his powers: The liquid movie is obviously in a different class from the lumpy play. In one respect, though, Hernandez' vision is more inclusive than Almodovar's; it finds a place for men, and -- Singkil revisionism notwithstanding --a generous one. Both are fundamentally warm-hearted works, but the play has structural cracks that make it feel chilly. - Until Jan. 28. 416-504-9971
